body:
Closes #227.

## The problem

`perform_grna_precomputation()` fits a logistic regression of the gRNA-presence indicator onto the covariate matrix, once per gRNA target per call. That fit depends on exactly two things: which cells contain the target, and the covariate matrix. It does not touch the response counts.

Any workflow that runs many analyses over the same cells and the same gRNA assignments while varying only the counts — a power simulation, for example — therefore refits an identical model on every call. `sceptre` already caches the *response* precomputation (`@response_precomputations`); the gRNA precomputation had no equivalent.

## The change

A `grna_precomputations` slot, symmetric with `@response_precomputations`: populated and reused automatically, and reset by `set_analysis_parameters()`, `assign_grnas()`, and `run_qc()`. It applies when `resampling_mechanism` is `"crt"`.

This is memoisation, not an approximation — the two inputs are invariant across the repeated calls, and the CRT resamples are redrawn on every call exactly as before.

Roughly 156 lines of executable R across six files. No new exports, no `NAMESPACE` change, no new `.Rd`.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `R/s4_class.R` | the slot |
| `R/precomputation_functions.R` | cache lookup, reconstruction from coefficients, freshness check, slot accessor |
| `R/association_testing_functions_v2.R` | the two CRT workhorses accept the cache and return their fit alongside the results |
| `R/medium_level_functs_v2.R` | merges the fits back from the `mclapply` workers |
| `R/s4_analysis_functs_2.R` | injects the cache on the CRT branch; one shared write-back helper |
| `R/s4_analysis_functs_1.R` | the resets |

### Design points

**Coefficients are cached, not fitted values.** The fitted values are one double per cell, so at realistic screen sizes the cache would exceed the data it summarizes; the coefficients are a handful of numbers per target, matching what `@response_precomputations` already stores. `glm.fit()` computes its fitted values as `linkinv(drop(x %*% coefficients))` and then strips the names, so reproducing both steps recovers them exactly. The test asserts `identical()` rather than `equal()` deliberately: a one-ulp difference would flip a Bernoulli draw in `crt_index_sampler_fast()` and move a p-value.

**Entries are fingerprinted by the index vector that determines the fit.** `crt_glm_factored_out()` regresses on every cell in use; `discovery_ntcells_crt()` regresses on `c(trt_idxs, all_nt_idxs)`. An entry cached by one is wrong in the other, and since both analyses share one cache a length check would not separate them. Comparing the index vector identifies the code path, the gRNA assignment, and the cell set in a single check. A stale entry is refit and replaced rather than raising, since the cache is package-maintained rather than user-supplied.

**`assign_grnas()` needed a wider reset than the response cache has.** The existing reset there is gated on `low_moi`, because reassignment perturbs the response precomputation only through `cells_in_use`. The gRNA fit regresses on the assignments themselves, so it must reset in either MOI.

**Only the fit is cached, never the synthetic index sets.** Caching `crt_index_sampler_fast()`'s output would freeze the resampling distribution across replicates and destroy the CRT null while still producing plausible-looking numbers. The two call sites carry a comment to that effect.

**`run_calibration_check()` neither reads nor writes the cache**, since its gRNA groups are randomly chosen sets of non-targeting gRNAs, resampled on every call. A calibration run leaves an existing discovery cache intact.

## Tests and checks

New `tests/testthat/test-grna_precomputations.R` (29 tests) covering: exact recovery of the fitted values from the coefficients; cache hit and cache miss agreeing bit-for-bit; stale entries being refit; rank-deficient fits being declined rather than cached; a `"complement"` cache transplanted into an `"nt_cells"` object changing nothing; the calibration check leaving the cache untouched; and the resets.

Both the test suite and `R CMD check --as-cran` were run against `main` and against this branch in the same environment:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| test suite | 2578 passed, 0 failed | 2607 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings |
| `R CMD check` | 1 WARNING, 3 NOTEs | 1 WARNING, 3 NOTEs (identical set) |

The WARNING and NOTEs are environmental — absent `qpdf`, installed package size, filesystem clock skew, top-level files — and are byte-identical between the two arms.

## Compatibility

Reads go through an accessor that falls back to `list()` via `methods::.hasSlot()`, so a `sceptre_object` serialized before the slot existed still analyzes; the slot materializes on first write.

## Statistical and behavioral implications

Numerical results are unchanged, which is what the `identical()` assertions pin down.

One user-visible change: a warning raised by the gRNA regression (for example, about fitted probabilities numerically equal to zero or one) is now emitted on the call that performs the fit rather than on every call that reuses it. There is a test for this and a note in `NEWS.md`.

title: Cache the gRNA precomputation on the sceptre_object
